The reviewer landed https://github.com/ihsan-sa/hive/pull/175, now merged, with this advice:

- DiffID replaces each hunk header with plain `@@`. So an identical added hunk with identical context, placed at a different spot in a file with repeated blocks, gets the same id. Consider keeping each hunk's position relative to the hunks before it, or the function-context part of the header.
- GitHub.Checks asks for check-runs and check-suites with per_page=100 and doesn't page further. A head with more than 100 runs would hide some of them; follow the Link header or the total_count.
- A PR whose mergeability stays UNKNOWN waits forever with no alert (the worker flagged this too). Raise one alert after a bound, as is done for checks queued over an hour.
- CI's `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` cancels the old head's run when a new head is pushed. That shows up as cantstart, so a superseded head could raise main-red. Today t.SHA has always moved on by then, but skipping or ignoring cancellations on heads that are no longer the task's would keep alerts clean.
- A clean PR now merges onto a main the Hive never tested it with, and the PR CI tested it against an older main. Consider re-running the Hive's own test on the combined tree, or turning on GitHub's 'require branches up to date' rule for the self repo. That trades CI restarts for safety, and lessons.md already has one 'red after merge' revert (#163).
- When the forge reports a PR's mergeability as UNKNOWN (or empty), `upToDate` waits with no alert. Raise one alert after a bound, for example 30 minutes.
- With `--binary`, git may write a binary change as a delta against the old blob. `DiffID` drops the blob ids, so in principle two delta patches from different old blobs could share an id. Hashing binary patches with their index lines kept would close that.
- A check run cancelled by the ci.yml concurrency group on the same head counts as can't-start and holds until someone reruns it. Consider re-requesting the run once automatically before raising the alert.
- `Local.refresh` now runs `git merge-tree` on every PR read. That's fine for tests, but it could be cached per head and main pair if dev runs get slow.
- A clean PR now merges onto a main the Hive never tested it with, which is the kind of failure behind the revert of #163 in lessons.md. Consider a light check before merging, for example running the tests on the merge-tree result with the newest main without pushing it, or rely on improve's after-merge measurement and say so in docs/risk.md.
- Reads() merges in the per-sha lands with the per-diff lands, but a fix on one head with diff D only clears the per-diff lands. A land recorded on an earlier head with the same diff still counts for that earlier sha. This is a narrow edge, but the fix should clear the per-sha lands too, so the two records can't disagree.
- A host-made revert of a change on the security list is now held for a perms or architect read, and must also pass the required GitHub checks, before it merges. Decide whether a revert should be exempt from the outside read, and at least raise an alert when one is held, so an urgent revert doesn't sit unnoticed.
- A long UNKNOWN mergeability, or a required check that never reports (for example a job rename in ci.yml), holds a PR with no alert. Consider raising one after an hour or so, as is already done for a check queued too long.
- GitHub.Checks has not run against the live API. Add a fakeGH test with recorded check-runs, status and check-suites JSON.
- Host-made reverts go through the same gate. A revert of a bad merge that touched a security-listed path (runs.go, harness) now waits for a perms or architect read, and for the GitHub checks, before it can undo the bad merge. Consider letting a host revert through the outside-read hold, since it restores code that was already read, or raise an alert so the person knows a revert is waiting.
- `Effects.Reads` joins the per-sha lands with the per-diff lands. A land on sha A followed by a fix on a later head B with the same DiffID clears only the per-diff list, so A still counts as read in a self or high-class project. Clear the per-sha lands of every head with that diff when a fix lands on it, or check the latest verdict on the diff first.
- `DiffID` drops the whole `@@` line, the function context included. The same added lines with the same context, moved to another spot in the same file, keep the read. Keeping the trailing function context after `@@`, or the order of hunks within each file, would narrow this.
- As the worker notes, a clean PR now merges onto a newer main that neither the Hive nor GitHub tested it with. Only the post-merge measurement and revert catch a semantic break. Consider having GitHub test the merge ref, or making the branch-up-to-date rule a project setting.
- `noteTests` keeps its own `ownDiff` hash (-U0, no renames) next to `core.DiffID`. Two names for 'this change's own diff' can drift apart; consider using `DiffID` for both.
- A Hive-made revert of a merge that touched a listed security path now holds until the person records a perms or architect read, so an improve revert of a bad security change can wait with nobody told. Consider raising an alert when a revert task is held this way, or deciding explicitly that reverts are exempt.
- A project with CI but no required_checks on main has nothing to hold the merge in the moments after a push, before GitHub has created the check suite, so it can merge before its CI has registered. Consider a short wait after a push, or a required_checks default.
- Once the forge reports UNKNOWN mergeability, the PR is held every minute with no PR line or alert (the worker listed this as unsure). Raise one if it lasts longer than a set time.
- A clean PR that merges as it is lands on a main the Hive never tested it against. Consider re-running the Hive's own test on the merged result (improve's measure-after-merge partly covers this), or recording it as a known gap in docs/risk.md.
- A clean PR now merges onto a main the Hive never tested it with, because main is merged in only on a conflict or when GitHub requires the branch to be up to date. GitHub's own `pull_request` CI runs on the PR merged with main as it was at push time, so it covers part of the gap. Still, measure how often post-merge reverts happen now (the #163 lesson). If they rise, consider a test-only check of the PR merged onto current main before merging, without pushing it.
- In `forgeChecks`, if main fails any one of the PR's failing checks, the whole PR waits on main, even when the PR fails other checks that main passes. Only the failures main shares should be excused; the rest should still go back to the worker.
- An UNKNOWN mergeable state that never resolves waits forever with no alert. Raise one after a bound, as for a check that can't start.
- Outside reads arrive only by the person's hand (`hive read`). Consider letting autobox's relayed PR comment be picked up, or at least showing the exact `hive read` command in the person's dashboard.
- Reads() combines land votes recorded per commit and per diff. A fix recorded at head B clears the land votes for B's diff, but an earlier head A with the same diff keeps its own per-commit lands. In a self project, A would still count as read after the fix. Have a fix on a diff also clear the per-commit lands for every head with that diff.
- When GitHub reports mergeability as UNKNOWN for a long time, the task keeps waiting with no reason saved and no alert. Raise an alert or save a reason after a few minutes.
- A clean PR now merges onto a main the Hive's own test never ran it with. GitHub's pull_request CI ran on a merge commit made when the PR was last pushed. Consider having the improve module's after-merge measurement flag this case, or require the forge's 'up to date' rule for self projects.
- The worker said they hadn't run GitHub.Checks and the mergeStateStatus field against the live API. Add a live probe or a fake-gh test of the three API calls.
- `hold` posts a new 'Holding the merge' comment every time the reason text changes. As pending checks finish one by one, the list of names changes, so a PR can get several comments in one wait. Consider leaving the changing check names out of the text that decides when to comment.
- `DiffID` drops `index` lines. A `--binary` delta patch is relative to the file's previous version (its preimage), so two different preimages with byte-identical deltas would get the same ID. This is unlikely, but it is worth recording next to the hunk-position limit in log.md, or keeping the preimage blob id for binary files.
- Protected-path approvals are still tied to the exact commit (`Approved("merge", sha)`), so every catch-up asks the person or warden again even when the own diff is unchanged. Binding approvals to `DiffID` like reads would match the new rule.
- `GitHub.Checks` hasn't been run against the live API. Run a probe on a real PR head (including a run attempted twice and `per_page` paging past 100 check runs) before relying on it.
- `noteTests`/`ownDiff` in work.go hash the own diff a second way (-U0, no binary). It works, but now that `core.DiffID` exists it's a second near-duplicate notion of 'own diff'. Consider folding it into DiffID so there's only one rule.
- A held task's next look is kept in memory only (`m.later`), and a check that stays pending raises no alert, so it can sit there indefinitely. Consider raising one alert when a required check stays pending past a set time (for example 2h).
- `GitHub.Checks` hasn't been run against the live API, and `required_checks` assumes the job is named 'test (ubuntu-latest)'. Run one live probe on an open PR to confirm both before relying on it.
- PR #149 got many reviewer runs; after merge, verify in events.jsonl that a catch-up no longer starts a reviewer run (the run id with `-read` suffix logic in `review` uses Reads with the diff, so it should be skipped at test()).
- Raise an alert when a merge stays held on pending forge checks past some hours; today a long hold is silent.
- Exercise GitHub.Checks once against the live API (pagination past 100 check runs, started_at on queued runs).
- Give the security seat its own prompt instead of the reviewer prompt plus a security brief.
- Build the tribunal panel for elevated-rights paths that goals.md's Security reads section asks for (filed as a follow-up).
- GitHub.Checks reads only the first 100 check runs and suites (per_page=100, no pagination). A head with more than 100 runs could miss a failure; follow the Link header or read total_count.
- A merge held on a pending check raises no alert however long it lasts. Raise one after a long hold, such as several hours, so a stuck required check doesn't stall a PR without anyone noticing.
- The `later` hold map lives only in memory, and `due` (whose caller holds m.mu) deletes from it. Note in its doc comment that `hold` must never be called with m.mu held, so a future change doesn't deadlock it.
- Test `GitHub.Checks` once against the live API, checking the real job names against `required_checks` ("test (ubuntu-latest)", "sandboxed-e2e"). A name mismatch would hold every merge forever.
- The worker pointed out that main now merges a PR as-is when GitHub reports it mergeable (upToDate), and does not catch it up with main and retest first. An earlier review round refused that. The lead or the person should decide it in its own brief.

tasks.title: Follow up the review of The host-python install root can't expose the workspace
tasks.done: Each item below is done, or judged not worth doing with the reason in your account.
tasks.known:
The reviewer landed https://github.com/ihsan-sa/hive/pull/217, now merged, with this advice:

- installRoot only turns down a root that contains a guarded path. It doesn't turn down one inside a covered folder, such as an interpreter installed under .hive/private/<agent home> or .hive/logins, which would be bound read-only and expose that subtree. That's unlikely from the daemon's PATH, but consider also refusing any root that holds(g, r) for the covered folders (not the workspace root, since an install inside the workspace is allowed on purpose).
- Guarding the workspace root already covers logins/modules/private, unless those folders are symlinked out of the workspace. A one-line comment on Workspace.Guarded saying that's why they're listed separately would stop a later simplification from dropping them.
- Run the sandbox e2e test (HIVE_E2E_SANDBOX=auto) once with a host python installed outside the system dirs, to confirm the bin-only fallback still starts inside.
- Make sure the PR asks for the perms or architect read that `.hive/goals.md` requires for sandbox changes before it merges.
- Consider an e2e or bwrap-level test that runs with a python outside the system dirs and the workspace beside it, to check the bind set inside a real sandbox and not only `installRoot`'s return value.
- The macOS sandbox profile isn't touched here. Check whether it has its own interpreter install-root logic that needs the same guard.
- Run the sandbox e2e suite (`HIVE_E2E_SANDBOX=auto go test ./internal/e2e/`) on a Linux host where python3 is outside the system dirs and the workspace is under that install's parent, to confirm the bin-only fallback still runs the interpreter end to end.
- Have the perms or architect read confirm the worker's two open questions: whether binding /data/bin alone (rather than dropping the interpreter entirely) counts as 'refused', and whether guarding every mount's host path is wanted.
- installRoot only checks whether a guarded path is under the candidate root, not the reverse. tasks.title: Follow up the review of Main's ci runs finish, and a job waiting on main uses the latest finished answer
tasks.done: Each item below is done, or judged not worth doing with the reason in your account.
tasks.known:
The reviewer landed https://github.com/ihsan-sa/hive/pull/385, now merged, with this advice:

- If none of the last 10 main commits has a finished run and main's newest run of the check was cancelled, MainAnswer falls back to main's own runs. ChecksAgainstMain then counts the cancelled run as 'main doesn't fail', and stillOnMain doesn't treat it as still going, so the PR's red goes back as the change's own right away. That is the old behaviour, and it's rare now that main runs aren't cancelled. To match 'a cancelled run is never an answer', the gate could treat a cancelled main run with no finished answer like a pending one and wait the usual 45 minutes, with a test for it.
- Tasks persisted before this change have MainWaitOn set to a main SHA, so their wait timer restarts once after upgrade. That's harmless, but worth knowing if a PR seems to wait longer than 45 minutes right after the release.
- When none of main's last 10 commits has a finished run of the check and main's newest run was cancelled, stillOnMain doesn't count it as still running. The PR's red then goes back as its own at once, so a cancelled run still decides the outcome in that fallback. Treating a cancelled main run as 'still waiting' (bounded by mainWaitMax) would close this. It matters little now that main's runs aren't cancelled.
- MainWait is keyed on the head SHA and never reset. If the checks on the same head are re-run, a later wait on main can start out already expired. Consider resetting it when a re-run starts.
- MainAnswer reads up to 10 extra check lists per red PR on every look while main's newest commit has no finished run. If forge rate limits ever bite, cache the answer per (main SHA, check).
- MainAnswer can miss a red that main picked up since the older finished commit. Consider logging which older commit the merge gate used, so a merge past a red check is auditable.
- The brief mentioned the Hive's own measure of main. The change leaves that out on purpose; a follow-up could say so in docs.
- MainAnswer swallows a rev-list error and silently falls back to main's own runs. A journal or log line when that happens would make a stale or missing project clone visible.
- If a security-relevant CI job is ever added to the required checks, think about whether its baseline should only ever be main's newest commit, so an older main answer can't excuse a red security check.
- Consider recording in the merge-gate journal event which older main commit MainAnswer used, so a merge that relied on a stale main answer can be audited.
